decisions.reason: Changing the proposal's brand identity does not alter the requirement to place photos in the final draft.
The complete-document layout and single-pass requirements remain valid unchanged under the new brand identity.
This Requirement is introduced by the same message and already reflects Blue Mesa identity and the prepared-for-client credit line; no additional modification is needed.
The switch to Blue Mesa branding does not change the requirement to provide editable Canva access and ownership.
The organization chart must still be applied to the final draft regardless of the branding identity.
The branding change does not alter integration of the supplied tables or budget sheet into the final draft.
The maximum page count remains an RFQ submission constraint and is unaffected by which organization supplies the branding.
The required print-ready PDF format remains unchanged after the branding switch.
Using the complete final draft as the content basis remains valid and does not depend on the selected brand identity.
The source decision concerns the separate Civic Canopy RFQ and Blue Mesa bidder identity, not the RCP proposal.
The source decision concerns a separate RFQ and has no effect on the RCP personnel materials.
The Blue Mesa branding decision for the RFQ does not alter source-file or PDF delivery requirements for the separate RCP proposal.
